content: Pyrazinamide is prescribed for the initial treatment of active tuberculosis in both adults and children. It is used in combination with other antituberculous medications to ensure effective therapy. For patients with drug-resistant tuberculosis, treatment regimens should be tailored to the specific resistance patterns and clinical circumstances of the individual. Pyrazinamide often plays a critical role as part of these customized treatment plans. In patients who have a concurrent HIV infection, clinicians must adhere to the latest guidelines provided by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). These patients may require an extended duration of treatment due to the complexity of their condition. Pyrazinamide is also indicated for use in cases where treatment with other first-line antituberculous drugs has failed, regardless of the form of active tuberculosis. It is important to note that pyrazinamide should always be administered in combination with other effective antituberculous agents to prevent the development of drug resistance and to ensure optimal therapeutic outcomes.
